transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I’ve been having trouble opening my bowels. It started about three weeks ago — I’m going much less often and I have to strain.
How has this been affecting your day-to-day life, and do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
The straining is uncomfortable — about 4 out of 10 — and my lower tummy feels bloated, which is bothering me day to day. I don’t have any known drug allergies.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started recently, and any health problems or operations you’ve had in the past?

I started co-codamol 30/500, two tablets four times a day, about a month ago for back pain. I also take apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day, bisoprolol 2.5 mg once a day, and a calcium and vitamin D chewable tablet twice a day. I have osteoarthritis in my spine and knees and an irregular heartbeat, and I haven’t had any operations.

Other than those, is there anything else you take — for your spine and knees or your irregular heartbeat, at other times of day, as inhalers, eye drops, creams, injections or patches, or anything bought without a prescription like painkillers, vitamins or herbal remedies? If not, that’s fine.

No, that’s everything — I don’t take anything else for my spine or knees or my heartbeat, and I don’t use inhalers, eye drops, creams, injections or patches. I don’t take any other painkillers, vitamins or herbal remedies bought without a prescription.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy since this started, or any changes in your bladder or bowel habits or your breathing?

I haven’t noticed any changes in my appetite, sleep, weight or energy. My bowels have changed, though — now I go about every 4–5 days, when normally it’s every day or every other day. I haven’t noticed anything different with my bladder or my breathing.
Is there anything you’ve noticed that seems to make opening your bowels easier or harder — such as food, drink, movement, or your medicines?
I haven’t noticed anything that makes it easier. I have been drinking less — about 3 cups of tea a day — because I don’t want to keep getting up at night.
Are there any other health conditions you see a doctor or nurse about regularly that we haven’t talked about?
No, there isn’t anything else I see a doctor or nurse about regularly that we haven’t already talked about — just the arthritis and the irregular heartbeat.
What worries you most about this, and what are you hoping we can do for you today?
I’d like something to get things moving again. What worries me most is whether this could be something serious, like bowel cancer.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed going on with your body alongside the trouble opening your bowels?
I haven’t noticed any blood in my stools, black stools, or vomiting. Apart from the bloating and straining, I haven’t noticed anything else going on.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
